# Lessons are built from open data, not generated by Claude

> Partly superseded by ADR 0011: Lesson text is now written fresh for OpenChessCoach rather than adapted from Wikibooks. The rules on open data, positions and credits still apply, and a note kept from Wikibooks keeps its credit.

Lesson content is assembled from open sources rather than invented by the Coach. Lichess's opening names (CC0) supply the catalogue of openings. Move statistics by rating band, computed in advance from the CC0 Lichess games database, supply "what players at your level play here". Terse notes adapted once from Wikibooks' *Chess Opening Theory* (CC BY-SA 4.0) supply the "why". Lichess's puzzle database (CC0) supplies Puzzles for practice afterwards. Generated lessons would cost tokens and could teach wrong lines. Lichess's own Learn content is AGPL and covers only the rules, and Lichess Practice has no opening lessons. Community Studies belong to their authors, so none of these can be bundled.

## Consequences

- The Wikibooks-derived notes we ship must credit Wikibooks and stay under CC BY-SA 4.0. That licence applies only to those notes, not to the app's code.
- The live Lichess Opening Explorer needs a Lichess sign-in for every request, so it can only be an optional extra later.
- The research behind this decision is in `docs/research/lesson-content-sources.md`.
